proposed_definition_changes.reason: The former remote-pair pass test unnecessarily required the whole product box to lie in the remote region. Positivity of the moment-distance enclosure on the whole box already certifies positivity on its remote subset, so the corrected one-sided rule preserves soundness and removes the boundary-straddling obstruction.

proposed_definition_changes.proposed: For \(p\geq3\) and fixed \(\iota\), enumerate the finite admissible input class in its prescribed deterministic order and run \(\mathfrak C(\Xi)\) on every input. Record every tri-valued status and its receipt, propagate the directed-rounding Taylor models and recursive Poisson tails through wrong-graph exclusion, one-sided remote-pair certification, local chart injectivity, Jacobian nonsingularity, covariance inversion, and designated-contrast precision, and retain as frontier candidates only nondominated inputs whose status is \(\mathtt{CERTIFIED}\). Inputs with status \(\mathtt{REFUTED}\) or \(\mathtt{UNDECIDED}\) remain recorded and are not promoted to certified designs.
proposed_definition_changes.reason: The handle must distinguish always-recorded tri-valued outcomes from the certified designs eligible for the Pareto frontier and must reflect the corrected one-sided remote-pair branch.

proposed.role: Published count-valued, causally minimal, pairwise-identifiable CPCM class; source-node laws are unrestricted.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The old symbol role incorrectly described the published CPCM class as the paper's Poisson-root positive-polynomial subclass.

proposed.construction: \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{CPCM}}=\{((P_r,d_r))_{r=1}^{K}:\text{ for every }r,\ P_r\in\mathcal P(\mathbb N_0^p)\text{ is generated by a causally minimal count-valued CPCM with labeled DAG }d_r\text{ in the sense of Definition 9 of Bodik--Chavez-Demoulin, and assumption }\mathrm{ass{:}pairwise\text{-}identifiability}\text{ holds in the sense of their Definition 10}\}\). No parametric restriction is imposed on a source-node law beyond being a probability law on \(\mathbb N_0\).

proposed_core_edits.reason: Definitions 9--10 of Bodik--Chavez-Demoulin define a broader count-valued, causally minimal, pairwise-identifiable CPCM class with arbitrary source-node laws. Poisson roots and positive-polynomial kernels belong only to this paper's strict benchmark subclass.

proposed.statement: Assume \(p\geq3\) and fix the ordered injection \(\iota:\{X,Y,Z\}\hookrightarrow\{1,\ldots,p\}\). If \(\operatorname{rank}(M)=K\) and every recovered component law belongs to \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{CPCM}}\), then the pooled-law tuple identifies each labeled type graph \(D_r\). If the recovered law belongs to \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{poly}}(\mathfrak G,\Theta,q)\), it also identifies the \(\iota\)-indexed contrast vector \(\boldsymbol\tau=((\tau_{i_Y,r},\tau_{i_Z,r}))_{r=1}^{K}\) through the displayed truncated factorization at \(V_{i_X}\).
proposed.justification: This theorem composes unrestricted labeled-law unpooling with the published direct-law CPCM identification result, while reserving intervention effects for the stricter positive-polynomial Poisson subclass.
proposed.gap: Bodik--Chavez-Demoulin identifies a causally minimal, pairwise-identifiable CPCM DAG from a direct joint law and permits arbitrary source-node laws; it does not recover labeled type laws from several known-composition pools. Gao--Cai--Hara and Luo--Sun--Zhang likewise do not supply that labeled multi-composition inverse.
proposed.consumer: It states exactly what a successful known-composition bulk assay identifies at the cellular causal level: broad-class labeled DAGs, but polynomial-subclass intervention contrasts.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The displayed claim is retained while its dependency spine is synchronized with the corrected published CPCM class definition; the new proof uses no Poisson-root restriction for the first DAG-identification clause.

proposed.comparator_claim: The paper uses cumulant or transform inversion to recover independent additive link-delay components from aggregate path measurements.
Theorems 1--2 identify component distributions up to shifts, and Section 4 estimates transform mixtures by GMM.
Theorem 2 obtains component recovery under pairwise column independence for a generalized-hyperexponential approximation class.
Definitions 9--10 define the causally minimal and pairwise-identifiable CPCM setting, allowing arbitrary source-node laws, and Lemma 11 identifies its DAG from the direct joint law.

Definition 3 specifies PT-SEM from direct observational count vectors; Theorem 12 identifies its DAG, thinning matrix, and node-wise exogenous distributions under (A1)--(A3), and Theorem 18 proves plug-in BIC selection consistency under (A1)--(A5).
Section 4.2 studies functional consistency under linear aggregation and gives affine ANM/PNL consequences; Section 4.3 concerns conditional-independence consistency.
The paper establishes consistency, asymptotic normality, and covariance weighting for finite or continuum moments.
The article develops mathematically rigorous verification methods based on directed floating-point and interval arithmetic.
The article distinguishes rigorous from non-rigorous deterministic branch-and-bound and reviews sound interval relaxations and termination claims.
The paper combines Taylor-model enclosures with branch-and-bound for rigorous global search.
The paper constructs rigorous interval quasiconvex relaxations for self-validating constrained global optimization.
Theorems 2 and 4 certify approximate polynomial roots and common associated roots.
The paper optimizes network-tomography probe allocation using Fisher information.

proposed_core_edits.reason: Bodik--Chavez-Demoulin is now matched directly by the causal-transfer theorem after labeled-law unpooling, rather than being recorded only as background inspiration; all other comparator positions are unchanged.

prose_updates.tldr: Known linearly independent raw-count compositions recover unrestricted labeled type laws for arbitrary \(p\geq1\) by a logarithmic count-PGF inverse, with positive Poisson aliases proving necessity. Any recovered count-valued law in the published pairwise-identifiable CPCM class then has its labeled DAG identified; intervention contrasts and validation use the stricter compact positive-polynomial Poisson subclass. For \(p\geq3\), the headline is a finite sound tri-valued certifier: it always terminates, and only a \(\mathtt{CERTIFIED}\) output verifies a rational chart-projection cover together with wrong-graph separation, global within-graph injectivity, local Jacobian nonsingularity, interiority, PGF-tail, and designated-contrast precision bounds. The finite-grid theorem separately proves existence of some finite rational grid and cover with positive exact margins; it does not certify either prescribed synthetic input. Pointwise sample-split Wald inference is conditional on certification, the capped certified-design frontier is finite, and the three-node base/conditional-refinement benchmark status remains open.

project_justification.gap: Transform inversion, direct-law CPCM identification, and validated numerics are established separately. The published CPCM result starts from a direct count-valued joint law and allows arbitrary source-node distributions; it does not recover labeled type laws through known multi-composition pools, while existing validated-numerics results do not jointly propagate infinite-support PGF tails through graph, global-injectivity, local-regularity, and causal-precision checks.
project_justification.niche: Prospective known-composition designs need a proof-producing bridge from aggregate raw-count laws to labeled cellular laws and then to the broadest justified graph class, with stricter intervention and inference claims explicitly confined to a certifiable polynomial subclass.
project_justification.fill: The project composes the arbitrary-dimensional rank frontier with published pairwise-identifiable CPCM DAG recovery, then supplies for \(p\geq3\) an always-terminating sound tri-valued certifier and a finite capped design frontier for the compact positive-polynomial Poisson subclass. Relative eventual certification requires strict exact graph, remote, local, interiority, and precision slack together with convergent truncation, Taylor, subdivision, and outward-rounding controls; no prescribed synthetic input is asserted certified.

sampling_model.design: Independent replicate wells are collected at fixed, known integer composition rows of \(M\), with exact raw-count addition and no unknown thinning or normalization. The two-row matrix \(M_0\) and both prescribed three-node inputs are synthetic prospective designs whose certification status remains open.
sampling_model.treatment: For \(p\geq3\), the ordered embedding \(\iota:\{X,Y,Z\}\hookrightarrow\{1,\ldots,p\}\) is fixed before analysis. Broad published-class membership is used only for labeled-DAG recovery. The interventions \(\operatorname{do}(V_{i_X}=1)\) and \(\operatorname{do}(V_{i_X}=2)\), and responses \(V_{i_Y}\) and \(V_{i_Z}\), are evaluated by truncated factorization only in the causally sufficient compact positive-polynomial Poisson subclass.
sampling_model.overlap: Positive Poisson roots and rates give full support on \(\mathbb N_0^p\) in the strict benchmark subclass, so every parent configuration used in its truncated-factorization functional has positive observational probability. No such Poisson-root or full-support claim is imposed on the broader published CPCM class used only for graph recovery.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Pooled PGFs are empirical replicate-well averages; component PGFs use the full-rank log inverse; graph and parameter estimates use the deterministic lexicographic sample-split selector. The certifier always returns one of three statuses, but inference is activated only by \(\mathtt{CERTIFIED}\), after normalized positive row allocation, wrong-graph separation, global within-graph injectivity, local nonsingularity, positive interiority clearance, tail control, and precision have all been verified.

prose_updates.related_work: Shih--Hero is credited at the source-verified level for transform inversion of independent additive link delays; the integer-multiplicity multivariate count-PGF inverse and positive unrestricted converse are derived here. Bodik--Chavez-Demoulin Definitions 9--10 describe the causally minimal, pairwise-identifiable CPCM setting, with arbitrary source-node laws, and Lemma 11 identifies its labeled DAG from the direct joint law. The present causal-transfer theorem strictly composes that direct-law result with labeled recovery from several linearly independent known-composition pools. Poisson roots, positive-polynomial non-root rates, intervention contrasts, finite-grid validation, certification, and Wald inference remain this paper's narrower benchmark layer. Gao--Cai--Hara identifies Poisson-thinning structural models from direct count vectors, not labeled laws through known multi-composition pools. Luo--Sun--Zhang Sections 4.2--4.3 study preservation of functional or conditional-independence structure under a fixed aggregation, not inversion using multiple labeled composition rows. Chen--Cao--Bu, Thoppe, Carrasco--Florens, and Newey--McFadden supply transform, tomography, minimum-distance, and extremum ingredients. Rump, Kearfott, Berz--Makino, Jansson, and Hauenstein--Sottile inform directed rounding, interval global search, Taylor enclosures, relaxations, and local root checks. The new validation ingredient is their joint use with analytic Poisson-PGF tails, one-sided remote-pair branching, a verified chart-projection cover, covariance propagation, and designated causal precision.
prose_updates.interpretation: Full column rank first identifies each labeled cellular observational law and nothing causal is defined by that inverse. On the published count-valued, causally minimal, pairwise-identifiable CPCM class, the recovered law then determines its labeled DAG even when source-node laws are non-Poisson. The designated intervention contrasts are a further conclusion only for the causally sufficient positive-polynomial Poisson subclass, where full support identifies every kernel entering the truncated factorization. A finite certificate is therefore evidence about one declared subclass and design, not a prerequisite for the population rank frontier or the broad-class law-to-DAG transfer.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The \(27\)-point floating-point pilot is not a certificate. Its two local Jacobian singular values are approximately \(0.00326480\) and \(0.00262027\), but it checks neither all wrong-graph and remote boxes nor chart coverage, tail error, rigorous covariance, or useful propagated precision. The finite procedure always terminates, yet may return \(\mathtt{UNDECIDED}\); relative eventual certification is available only under strict exact margins and convergent truncation, Taylor, subdivision, and outward-rounding controls. Neither the base input nor its one permitted refinement is presently certified.
prose_updates.honest_scope: Unrestricted rank recovery and stability apply for arbitrary \(p\geq1\). Labeled-DAG transfer applies to recovered count-valued laws in the published causally minimal, pairwise-identifiable CPCM class and imposes no Poisson source law. Intervention contrasts, finite-grid existence, certification, benchmark precision, and Wald inference remain confined to the compact causally sufficient positive-polynomial Poisson subclass and, for the designated contrasts, require \(p\geq3\) and the fixed ordered embedding \(\iota\). Certification is sound and always terminating but may be undecided; an eventual-certification conclusion is relative to strict exact graph, remote, local, interiority, and precision slack and convergent numerical controls, and it does not certify either prescribed synthetic benchmark. Covariance and Wald claims additionally require normalized strictly positive sampled-row fractions and give pointwise, not uniform post-selection, coverage. No claim covers unknown thinning, normalization, composition error, shared well noise, hidden types, high-dimensional growth, or biologically calibrated coefficient boxes.
